clue.text: Henman's outgrown his favourite surface…

definitions.meaning: Tim Henman, the British tennis player, goes by a short name; grown out to full length, Tim becomes the longer form of the name
Henman played best on grass courts, and this is a kind of meadow grass grown for hay

explanation.surface: A tennis star has moved on from the court he once loved best.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into 5 across. Tim Henman was a British tennis player best known for his runs at Wimbledon, which is played on grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is the full name that Tim abbreviates, and timothy is also a common pasture grass.

clue.text: Check and dress down

definitions.meaning: to mark an item on a list as done

explanation.definitionFit: To tick off is to mark items as checked, and also British slang for to scold.

clue.text: The view is not so good from up here

definitions.text: The view is not so good from up here

parts.words: The view is not so good from up here
parts.note: seems to be about a poor view from a hilltop, but means opinions held from a position of claimed virtue look smug

explanation.definitionFit: Taking the high moral position means claiming superior virtue, a view others find unappealing.

clue.text: Grade and transitive rating put over it are set at meal times

annotationWithheld.why: Grade and transitive rating put over it are set at meal times (9): definition is 'set at meal times' but no parse of 'Grade and transitive rating put over it are' giving the letters of the answer could be found or confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Grade and transitive rating put over it are set at meal times

clue.text: I'm certain arrival will be in 730 days, minimum

indicators.note: will be in places the arrival letters inside the affirmation

parts.note: yes is a firm affirmation, as if saying I am certain
ar. is an abbreviation for arrival in timetables

explanation.surface: A confident prediction that someone will turn up in two years at the very least.
explanation.walkthrough: 730 days is two years, the fewest that a plural count of years can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Years in the plural means at least two, and two of them make 730 days.

clue.text: … overheads sorted by one who's charming

definitions.meaning: in tennis an overhead is a high ball hit downwards hard; a player who deals with overheads that way smashes them
an informal British word for a very attractive or delightful person

explanation.surface: Continuing the tennis theme: the charming player who puts away the overhead shots.
explanation.walkthrough: Read on from 1 across: Henman's overheads are sorted by someone who smashes them. The second sense is informal British slang for someone gorgeous.
explanation.definitionFit: One who smashes is literally a smasher, and the word is also British slang for an attractive, delightful person.

clue.text: Inverted danger sign is taking in African runner — this man withdraws competitor

indicators.note: in a down clue, inverted means the whole built word is turned upside down
taking in means holding inside, so the river goes inside

parts.note: red is the colour that signals danger
a river runs, and the Nile is in Africa
taken as written

explanation.surface: An upside-down warning sign, an African athlete and a man who pulls a competitor out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taking in' puts NILE inside REDIS to give RENILEDIS, and 'Inverted' turns that over.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sidelines someone, removing them from the action, is a sideliner.

clue.text: 18, generally, had ultimatum spelled out

indicators.note: the run of letters is spelt out within the words had ultimatum

explanation.surface: An eighteen-year-old was given an ultimatum.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighteen is generally the age at which a person legally becomes a grown-up.

clue.text: Vanadium and aluminium would not individually be so called

definitions.text: Vanadium and aluminium would not individually be so called

parts.words: Vanadium and aluminium would not individually be so called
parts.note: the symbols V and Al together make VANDAL, a hooligan; each separately is a chemical element

explanation.walkthrough: V (vanadium) plus Al (aluminium) spells VANDAL; only together are they a lout, so neither alone is that kind of element.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooligan element is a rowdy section of a crowd; taken together V and Al make a vandal.

clue.text: Pre-piper Hamelin defection?

parts.note: before the Pied Piper came, Hamelin was overrun with vermin, so it was a place where rats bred; defection is ratting

explanation.walkthrough: In the legend Hamelin was infested with rats until the Pied Piper led them away; to rat is also to defect.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattery is a place where rats are kept or bred, as Hamelin was before the Piper came.

clue.text: Character excluded by committee?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the committee piece sits beside the excluded piece

parts.note: a card is an eccentric, amusing person, a real character
a board is a governing committee
cut out means left out or excluded

explanation.surface: Someone left off the list by a committee's decision.
explanation.walkthrough: A cardboard cutout is a flat, lifeless figure, the sort of character a committee might push aside; the whole clue both builds and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard cutout is a flat stand-in figure, so a character with no real life who can be set aside at will.

clue.text: Stan's mate's happier when Junior's not around

indicators.note: not around says the junior's letters are absent, taken out of the happier word

parts.note: jollier means merrier, happier
Jr is the standard abbreviation for Junior

explanation.surface: Stan's friend cheers up whenever the youngster is out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan Laurel's comedy partner was Oliver Hardy, called Ollie. Removing JR from JOLLIER leaves the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Hardy, known as Ollie, was the partner of Stan Laurel in the Laurel and Hardy comedy duo.

clue.text: Keeping it dry, badly lose patience

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the reworked word holds the other pieces
done badly, the letters of lose fall into the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
to air washing is to dry it

explanation.surface: Someone stays dry-eyed but loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping it dry' reads as staying dry-eyed, but 'dry' is the verb air. 'badly' makes SOLE. Patience is the British name for the card game Americans call solitaire.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire is another name for the one-player card game known in Britain as patience.

clue.text: I'm seen on the Lagoon far too pickled with gin

indicators.note: pickled means drunk, so the letters are in a confused state

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone on the Venetian lagoon has had far too much gin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lagoon is the Venetian lagoon, where this old type of Venetian sailing vessel was used; the clue speaks as the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigatoon was a Venetian vessel, so it would be seen on the lagoon around Venice.

clue.text: Here when one's imprisoned, be let out with difficulty

definitions.text: Here when one's imprisoned, be let out with difficulty

indicators.note: imprisoned means shut inside, so the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
with difficulty suggests the letters are struggled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In this dungeon, a prisoner is let out only with great difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' rearranges BE LET OUT, and 'imprisoned' puts I inside. An oubliette is a dungeon reached through a trapdoor.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon entered from above, a place where a prisoner was kept.

clue.text: Nobody kept one!

parts.note: seems to say no person ever wrote one, but refers to the Grossmiths' comic novel in which a nobody records his daily life

explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody is a classic English comic novel by George and Weedon Grossmith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grossmiths' book is presented as the daily journal of Mr Pooter, a self-important nobody.

clue.text: Is hospital in Washington reluctant to get cleaner?

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside Washington

parts.note: DC, District of Columbia, stands for Washington
taken as written
loth means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Is a Washington hospital unwilling to take on a cleaner?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person; it is a cloth for washing dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishcloth is a cloth used for cleaning dishes, so a cleaner in the sense of a cleaning tool.

clue.text: It's yellow or red and right in the line of fire

indicators.note: in places the right letter inside the line

parts.note: the oche is the line a darts player throws from

explanation.surface: Something coloured and standing right in the firing line.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the line behind which a darts player stands to throw, so a jokey 'line of fire'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment that comes in yellow and red shades.

clue.text: Presumably some work by Spenser, say, to superintend

annotationWithheld.why: Presumably some work by Spenser, say, to superintend (7): 'to superintend' defines the answer, but how 'Presumably some work by Spenser, say' gives it could not be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Presumably some work by Spenser, say, to superintend

clue.text: Take best 9 variations from this composer

indicators.note: variations are altered versions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is short for recipe, Latin for take, as written on prescriptions
taken as written
the number written out as a word

explanation.surface: Choose the nine finest variations by this composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variations' rearranges R, BEST and NINE. R for 'take' comes from the Latin recipe heading on prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bernstein was an American composer, best known for West Side Story.

clue.text: Thleepth thoundly, having taken a distillate

indicators.note: soundly said with a lisp, here meaning as heard, so the lisped word is taken by its sound

parts.note: sleeps said with a lisp; sleeps means naps, which a lisp turns to napth
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lisps that they sleep soundly after taking a distilled spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The lisp turns S into TH: 'Thleepth' is 'sleeps', giving NAPS lisped as NAPTH, and 'thoundly' (soundly) says take that by ear, as NAPHTH. Add A.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a flammable liquid obtained by distilling petroleum or coal tar.

clue.text: One such as yourself left cracking The Listener (an obsession)

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the left letter goes inside

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed by it

explanation.surface: Someone working on The Listener crossword has become obsessed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard crossword series, so the surface pictures a solver. 'cracking' puts L inside EARTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthling is a human being, an inhabitant of Earth, as the solver is.

clue.text: Fuss caused when one surprised expression interrupts another

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so the first cry goes inside the second

parts.note: ha is another such exclamation
ooh is a cry of surprise

explanation.surface: A commotion begins when one gasp cuts into another.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoo-ha is an informal word for a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Flash Gordon's top male operative

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
operative means at work, so the letters are working into a new order

explanation.surface: Flash Gordon is the leading man and an agent in action.
explanation.walkthrough: Flash Gordon is the comic-strip space hero, so 'Flash' seems part of his name. 'operative' turns the four letters of 'male' into LEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief flash of light.

clue.text: Vulgar fellow inhaling drug

indicators.note: inhaling means taking in, so the drug goes inside the fellow

parts.note: a chap is a fellow, a man
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A crude man is breathing in narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap can mean tawdry or in poor taste, a synonym of vulgar.

clue.text: Unplanned jet carries their sign

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so the jet surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a spurt is a jet of liquid
of them means belonging to them, their
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: An unscheduled jet aircraft bears its owners' emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' looks like an aeroplane, but it is a gush of water, and 'carries' splits it to hold the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Spur-of-the-moment is an idiom for impulsive, done without planning.

clue.text: Few survivors on board now the battle's nearly done

definitions.text: Few survivors on board now the battle's nearly done

parts.words: Few survivors on board now the battle's nearly done
parts.note: seems to describe a ship after a sea battle, but the board is a chessboard with few pieces left as the game nears its end

explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; it is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the final stage of a chess game, when few pieces remain on the board.

clue.text: Sage Derby, say, Mum's swallowing

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so mother encloses the hat

parts.note: mama is a word for mother
a derby is a bowler hat, so an example of a hat

explanation.surface: A cheese called Sage Derby is being eaten by Mum.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage Derby is an English cheese marbled with sage, so 'Sage' looks like part of it. 'Derby' is the American word for a bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian title for a wise and holy person, a sage, as with Gandhi.
